doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Booking his own work and how Maynard got started
summary: His wife helps him book; he recalls Joe Glaser getting Maynard work and calls the business a crap shoot.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah. You do your own booking? Your own business?
Yeah, my wife helps me with that. My wife’s a publicist.

And she helps me when she can but it’s very difficult. I think you really need a high powered booking agent. It’s like when Maynard started he had Joe Glaser from ABC Booking and the way Maynard got started was that Joe would call these people and say, “you want Miles in there for a couple of weeks?” And they’d say, “yeah, I’d love to have him.” “Well how about Maynard Ferguson?” “No, never heard of him.” And Joe would say, “if you want Miles, you’ll take Maynard too.” And they got him. Of course Joe and a lot of these bookers also were capable of putting people face down in the local river if they had to, too. That was kind of a hold over from the depression I think. But now there’s so many people that want to work, that want to do things, and if you look, you being a saxophone player and a musician, if you look out there you can see that some of them deserve to be working and some of them don’t. It’s a crap shoot really, and it’s not so much gee I play good or I want to work a lot or I want to record a lot, a lot has to do with this or who you know and so forth. So that’s just the way it is.
